# Competitors

| Name | Website | One line | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| Deloitte | deloitte.com | Large consultancy selling AI strategy, governance and change programmes to enterprises. | Direct |
| TechCXO | techcxo.com | Fractional Chief AI Officers who lead AI strategy, governance and transformation part-time. | Direct |
| Paul Okhrem | paul-okhrem.com | Solo fractional Chief AI Officer for CEOs, plus ISO 42001 readiness consulting. | Direct |
| Accorian | accorian.com | Cybersecurity and compliance firm that sells ISO 42001 readiness and AI governance. | Indirect |
| Do it in-house | n/a | Executives and internal teams run AI strategy, policy and adoption themselves with no outside help. | Status quo |

## Why these
- **Deloitte:** Deloitte offers AI risk management and governance for scaling enterprise AI. It also sells organizational design, culture and change management to drive enterprise-wide AI adoption. A buyer who wants a big, safe brand for the same work Acme Advisory does would shortlist it. Acme Advisory's edge is a named senior person, not a team of juniors. That is my inference, not a sourced claim.
- **TechCXO:** It offers part-time Fractional Chief AI Officers who drive AI strategy, governance and transformation. This is the closest model to hiring one expert for a bounded engagement. A buyer weighing "one senior advisor versus a full-time hire" would compare it with Acme Advisory.
- **Paul Okhrem:** He is a solo operator selling to the same buyer. He is a part-time AI executive who owns AI strategy, governance, vendor decisions and board reporting. His terms are a written part-time mandate with a published six-month minimum. His ISO 42001 work is priced at USD 1,000 per hour with an 80-hour minimum. A buyer comparing individual experts would see him next to Acme Advisory.
- **Accorian:** It covers only the compliance slice of Acme Advisory's offer. Its ISO 42001 services run from scoping and gap assessment through AIMS development, policy and control work, and certification readiness. A buyer who only needs ISO 42001 would pick a specialist like this over a generalist advisor.
- **Do it in-house:** This is the most likely real alternative for many buyers. Acme Advisory's own site says most AI rollouts fail because the organization wasn't led through the change. That tells me the buyer's default is to keep going without outside help. The main cost to the buyer is a stalled rollout and unreviewed tools, not a fee.

## Notes
- Assumption: the company profile left "What they sell" blank. I used Acme Advisory's website, which describes an AI consulting practice helping executives and their organizations lead AI transformation. The site also lists AI sales enablement and ISO 42001 governance work.
- Not found: any named competitors from the founder, and any competitor for the AI sales enablement offer that I could verify. I left that offer out of the table.
